skill.description: Advanced TypeScript and JavaScript assistance for type modeling, strict configuration, migrations, build diagnostics, module issues, and code review.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown fences, TypeScript template literal syntax, example URLs, and stderr redirection. The remaining confirmed issues are legitimate command execution guidance and a diagnostic Python script that runs shell commands in the target project.

remediation.issue: The diagnostic helper uses subprocess.run with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell=True commands with argument arrays, add timeouts, and avoid shell pipelines where possible.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends npm, npx, node, ts-node, and migration commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running commands and describe whether each command reads, writes, installs, or executes project code.

remediation.issue: The cache cleanup guidance uses rm -rf on hidden build cache paths.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before deletion and prefer safer project scripts or explicit cache path confirmation.

content.value_statement: TypeScript projects often struggle with strict typing, slow builds, and complex migrations. This skill provides practical diagnosis, review checklists, and solution patterns for modern TypeScript work.
actual_capabilities: Reviews TypeScript configuration for strictness, module settings, path aliases, and performance flags.
Explains advanced type patterns such as branded types, conditional types, mapped types, and template literal types.
Diagnoses common compiler errors, module resolution issues, and slow type checking workflows.
Guides incremental JavaScript to TypeScript migration planning and tool selection.
Provides TypeScript code review criteria for type safety, module structure, and error handling.
Includes a diagnostic helper script for local TypeScript project inspection.
limitations: Shell commands in the guidance require user review before execution.
It does not replace specialized bundler, compiler internals, or deep module migration experts.
Example configurations need adaptation to each project before use.
The diagnostic script assumes common Node.js and TypeScript project layouts.

use_cases.title: Tighten TypeScript Strictness
use_cases.description: Audit compiler settings and prioritize safer strict mode options without breaking the project at once.

use_cases.title: Plan a Migration
use_cases.description: Create a staged JavaScript to TypeScript migration plan with practical checks and risk controls.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Slow Builds
use_cases.description: Review compiler diagnostics, monorepo structure, and configuration choices that affect type checking speed.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my TypeScript configuration for strictness, module settings, and safe defaults. Explain the highest priority changes first.

prompt_templates.title: Explain This Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me understand this TypeScript compiler error. Identify the likely cause, the safest fix, and any tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an incremental JavaScript to TypeScript migration plan for this project. Include validation steps and rollback points.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Type Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this TypeScript project for slow type checking. Prioritize compiler settings, type complexity, and monorepo structure.

output_examples.input: Review a tsconfig for a React app that recently enabled strict mode.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review explaining which strict settings are ready, which changes need staged rollout, and which files may need fixes.

output_examples.input: Diagnose a module resolution error in a monorepo package.
output_examples.output: A short cause analysis covering path aliases, package boundaries, runtime resolution, and the safest validation command.

output_examples.input: Plan migration of several JavaScript folders to TypeScript.
output_examples.output: A staged migration plan with file order, compiler settings, type coverage goals, and test checkpoints.

best_practices: Start with existing project scripts and configuration before proposing new tools.
Validate type changes with one-shot checks and avoid long-running watch commands.
Prefer simple types first, then introduce advanced type utilities only when they reduce real risk.
anti_patterns: Do not copy strict configuration templates without checking project module and build settings.
Do not run migration or package commands without reviewing their effects first.
Do not solve every modeling problem with complex conditional or mapped types.

faq.question: What problems does this skill handle best?
faq.answer: It works best for TypeScript configuration, compiler errors, type design, migrations, and build performance diagnosis.

faq.question: Can it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill includes command suggestions, but users should review commands before execution in their project.

faq.question: Does it support monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes project reference guidance, tooling comparison, and monorepo validation patterns.

faq.question: Can it help migrate JavaScript to TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides staged migration guidance, strictness rollout advice, and tool recommendations.

faq.question: Is it focused only on frontend TypeScript?
faq.answer: No. The guidance applies to frontend, backend, libraries, and Node.js TypeScript projects.

faq.question: When should I use another specialist?
faq.answer: Use a specialized expert for deep bundler internals, compiler internals, or complex ESM and CJS migration analysis.
